title: Medicare Advantage contractor, resident-harm, and enforcement bridge
purpose: Move the rev0374 appeal-burden pilot toward the missing harm/remedy/accountability row by preserving contractor identity, nursing-home-resident vulnerability, approved-authorization stability, concurrent-decision appeal rights, and CMS enforcement rails.
why_this_is_riskiest: Appeal metrics can still be averaged away. The most severe unfinished risk is that vulnerable post-hospital patients and contractor-reviewed requests experience different denial patterns, while audits/enforcement may remain disconnected from beneficiary remedy.

substantive_records.source_locator: HHS-OIG SNF report, What OIG Found bullets on naviHealth and contractors, accessed 2026-06-18.
substantive_records.bounded_inference: Contractor identity is not an implementation footnote. It must be a row key because one contractor handled roughly half of SNF admission requests and had a higher denial rate than internal MAO processing or other contractors, with nearly all appealed denials overturned.
noncertification_limits: single month and 19-MAO review
does not give request-level beneficiary outcomes
does not prove every naviHealth denial was wrong
does not connect to contract-specific enforcement or financial restoration

substantive_records.source_locator: HHS-OIG SNF report, What OIG Found bullet on nursing-home residents, accessed 2026-06-18.
substantive_records.bounded_inference: The row contract must retain residence/status and post-hospital vulnerability dimensions; a national or contract aggregate can hide a roughly 3.6x denial-rate differential for nursing-home residents.
noncertification_limits: does not determine clinical correctness of each denial
does not measure downstream care delay, rehospitalization, mortality, or out-of-pocket loss
does not establish the denominator across all MA contracts

substantive_records.period: 2026 OIG recommendation based on June 2024 review
substantive_records.bounded_inference: OIG’s recommendation to regularly collect request-level prior-authorization data with service type and contractor information confirms that rev0373/rev0375 row keys are not optional extras.
noncertification_limits: CMS did not explicitly concur or nonconcur with the three SNF recommendations on the report page
recommendation is not the same as implemented data release
does not itself provide request-level rows

substantive_records.source_locator: CMS CY2026 MA/Part D final-rule fact sheet, Enhancements to Medicare Advantage and Medicare Part D, accessed 2026-06-18.
substantive_records.bounded_inference: Approved inpatient authorizations need their own stability/remedy field: CMS says plans generally must honor approved inpatient admissions and may reopen only for obvious error or fraud.
noncertification_limits: rule text is not an observed implementation outcome
does not measure how often approvals are reopened, delayed, or honored
does not establish beneficiary restoration after improper reopening

substantive_records.source_locator: CMS CY2026 MA/Part D final-rule fact sheet, Closing MA Appeals Loopholes bullets, accessed 2026-06-18.
substantive_records.bounded_inference: Concurrent decisions and provider-submitted requests must be captured as appeal-rights events; otherwise ongoing-course-of-treatment denials can evade the row contract.
noncertification_limits: rule obligation is not compliance proof
does not prove timely notice, comprehension, appeal initiation, or care continuation
does not quantify plan-by-plan impact

substantive_records.source_locator: CMS Part C/D Program Audits page, program audit purpose/protocol caveat/downloads, accessed 2026-06-18.
substantive_records.bounded_inference: CMS program-audit protocols, results, and audit/enforcement reports are a required accountability input, but record layouts and protocols are audit/monitoring tools and cannot be treated as policy interpretation or beneficiary remedy proof.
noncertification_limits: page does not itself provide all audit-result rows
protocols are not a substitute for law/regulation review
audit findings need to be joined to contract, service, denial, harm, and remedy outcomes

substantive_records.source_locator: CMS Part C/D Enforcement Actions page authority/action-type section and recent-action list, accessed 2026-06-18.
substantive_records.bounded_inference: CMS has a live enforcement rail—CMPs, intermediate sanctions, and terminations—but the MA certification row must show whether enforcement links to the same contract/service denial pattern and produces beneficiary/provider restoration.
noncertification_limits: many recent actions are listed under broad contract-administration bases
enforcement amount is not necessarily beneficiary restoration
list alone does not identify improper denial/harm causality

false_pass_blocks: No contractor-average pass: contractor identity and parent/delegated-entity control must remain row keys.
No resident-average pass: nursing-home-resident and post-hospital vulnerability differentials must not be pooled away.
No rule-existence pass: CY2026 approved-authorization and appeal-rights rules are obligations, not observed compliance.
No audit-protocol pass: CMS audit protocols/record layouts are monitoring tools and not policy interpretation or remedy proof.
No enforcement-list pass: CMPs/sanctions/terminations must be joined to the same contract/service denial pattern and restoration outcome.
No beneficiary-remedy pass unless care/service continuation, time-to-relief, and financial restoration are populated.
next_minimum_viable_row: One SNF contract-month row with contractor/delegated-entity identity, nursing-home-resident flag, approval/reopening/concurrent-decision fields, request/denial/appeal/overturn counts, notice dates, time-to-care, service furnished, provider/payment restoration, program audit finding, enforcement action, and quality/RADV context.
